newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CRUDE OUTLOOK: Sell-off leaves market in flux.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CRUDE OUTLOOK: Sell-off leaves market in flux.

text.p: U.S. crude prices were thrown into a state of flux last week, as outright values declined $1.86 a barrel for the March spot NYMEX futures contract, leaving many traders anticipating an early week correction.
Thus far, the selling has won out over technicians looking for a paper market recovery, with the March NYMEX down an additional 25-40 cents Monday morning.
"I thought it was all oversold in the crude complex, but everything is up in the air right now," said a crude trader.

Weather patterns producing warmer temperatures along the key heating oil belt in the U.S. Northeast have not favored the products. In addition, expectations for an early spring rally for gasoline have faded with the output of recent, bearish inventory data, traders said.

For the cash grade markets, the last few sessions have featured improving values for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels, a trend expected to continue as long as LLS remains cheaper than trans-Atlantic crudes.

"You should see the sweet grades get stronger, with the numbers for bringing over the Brent leaving the arb at only around $1.00 or $1.05. At those levels there won't be a lot of Brent coming over," said a Texas crude broker.
LLS started on Monday a few cents higher than last Friday's close, around 20-25 cents over the outright March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Traders said the stagnant performance in the Midland and Heavy Louisiana Sweet markets could run into this week, but uncertainty for other sweet grades was evident.
"We are really due for a pop in the outrights, but for the grades it is less certain," said a broker.
"Midland has been down for so long on heavy supplies and a real lack of buying interest above a 40 cents discount," said a trader.

West Texas Sour/Midland was seen testing more positive numbers, and started the week at around $2.20 under the WTI/Cushing marker for March barrels, and 20 cents stronger than those levels for the April market.
